name: Technique Chaining
description: Build short BJJ combinations around real defensive cues and shared controls. Practice the handoff between actions, including how to stop when the next move is unavailable.
summary: A useful technique chain connects an attack to a follow-up through a specific defensive cue and controls you can carry into the next action.
overview: Start with one transition between two moves you already know. The difficult part is often the handoff: which grip stays, which one changes, and whether the opening still exists when you arrive.
key_takeaways: Choose a first attack you can actually finish; otherwise the defense you want may never appear.
Name the cue for the second action and the connections it needs.
Practice the transition between the moves, including the moment you change a grip or body angle.
Include a stopping point: if the controls are gone, recover a workable position.
Keep the first version short enough to test against resistance before adding more branches.

bjj_applications.scenario: A closed-guard hip-bump attempt draws forward pressure
bjj_applications.application: If the partner drives back in with an accessible arm, a kimura or overhook entry may follow. Preserve control of the arm and distance; do not fall back expecting a grip you have not secured.
bjj_applications.outcome: The defense suggests a continuation, while the available connection determines which one fits.

bjj_applications.scenario: You sweep from butterfly guard and arrive on top
bjj_applications.application: Keep track of the arm and legs that can stop your progress. Establish balance and begin a familiar pass if the opponent’s legs remain between you.
bjj_applications.outcome: The sweep flows into the actual landing position instead of ending with an unnecessary release.

bjj_applications.scenario: A passing attempt succeeds and the bottom player turns away
bjj_applications.application: Stay connected to their upper body and hips before attempting a back take. If they return flat, settle the pin rather than chasing behind a turn that has ended.
bjj_applications.outcome: Your next action follows the escape that is present.

common_mistakes.mistake: Memorizing a long sequence with a cooperative partner
common_mistakes.consequence: The chain depends on defenses that may never happen in a round.
common_mistakes.correction: Test two actions with a partner who can choose whether and how to defend.

common_mistakes.consequence: The opponent can recover before the second attack starts.
common_mistakes.correction: Identify one useful connection to retain and practice changing the others around it.

training_exercises.name: Train the handoff
training_exercises.description: Choose two familiar actions and start just before the first meets its expected defense. Move into the second at a controlled pace, keeping the required connection. Reset when the second position is secured, the connection is lost, or either partner taps.
training_exercises.focus: Find the grip and angle change that links the moves.

training_exercises.name: Make the branch real
training_exercises.description: Start earlier in the same exchange. The defender may allow the first attack, use the expected defense, or disengage. Continue, switch, or recover accordingly; reset after a clear positional result or tap.
training_exercises.focus: Use a chain as a decision, not a script.

knowledge_assessment.question: What information should you know before adding a second attack?
knowledge_assessment.answer: The defense that makes it available, the controls it needs, and where you will recover if those controls disappear.
